gloss: to pass; to overtake; to outstrip

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {追|お}い{抜|ぬ}きませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {追|お}い{抜|ぬ}いていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {追|お}い{抜|ぬ}いていませんでした

definitions.explanation: To catch up with and move ahead of someone or something that was in front. Used for physical movement like running or driving.
To exceed someone in performance, ranking, or achievement. Used figuratively for competition, statistics, or progress.

examples.japanese: {前|まえ}の{車|くるま}を{追|お}い{抜|ぬ}いた。
examples.english: I passed the car in front.

examples.japanese: ゴール{手前|てまえ}で{一気|いっき}に{三人|さんにん}を{追|お}い{抜|ぬ}いた。
examples.english: I overtook three people all at once just before the finish line.

examples.japanese: {狭|せま}い{道|みち}で{無理|むり}に{追|お}い{抜|ぬ}こうとすると{危|あぶ}ない。
examples.english: It's dangerous to try to pass on a narrow road.

examples.japanese: {売上|うりあげ}で{先輩|せんぱい}を{追|お}い{抜|ぬ}いた。
examples.english: I surpassed my senior colleague in sales.

examples.japanese: この{国|くに}の{人口|じんこう}はやがて{隣国|りんごく}を{追|お}い{抜|ぬ}くだろう。
examples.english: This country's population will eventually surpass that of its neighbor.

examples.japanese: {後発|こうはつ}メーカーが{技術力|ぎじゅつりょく}で{大手|おおて}を{追|お}い{抜|ぬ}く{例|れい}は{珍|めずら}しくない。
examples.english: It's not uncommon for latecoming manufacturers to surpass major companies in technical capability.

notes:
Godan verb ({五段|ごだん}). Transitive — takes を for the person or thing being overtaken.

ASPECT (ている):
- {追|お}い{抜|ぬ}いた (completed the overtaking)
- {追|お}い{抜|ぬ}いている (has overtaken; is in a state of having passed)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {追|お}い{越|こ}す means the same but is slightly more common in everyday speech
- {追|お}い{抜|ぬ}く emphasizes fully passing and leaving behind, while {追|お}い{越|こ}す can suggest just moving ahead momentarily

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {車|くるま}を{追|お}い{抜|ぬ}く (to pass a car)
- {一気|いっき}に{追|お}い{抜|ぬ}く (to overtake in one burst)
- {売上|うりあげ}で{追|お}い{抜|ぬ}く (to surpass in sales)
